dek: Gane beat Hokit 48-47 at UFC 334, but the real story is an eye poke no ref called.

slides.label: The Bit
slides.text: Josh Hokit wore *goggles* all fight week, a joke about Gane's foul history. Then the joke wrote its own punchline.

slides.label: The Poke
slides.text: Early in Round 1, Gane's fingers caught Hokit's eye. Referee *Marc Goddard* saw no foul, gave no warning.

slides.label: 25 Minutes
slides.text: Hokit says he fought the next *25 minutes seeing triple*, yet still pinned the champ on the fence and bloodied him.

slides.label: The Scorecards
slides.text: All three judges scored it *48-47*. One single round split the champion from the challenger.

slides.label: The Ask
slides.text: Hokit didn't call Gane a cheater. He posted the screenshot and asked for an *immediate rematch*.

slides.label: The Pattern
slides.text: This is Gane's *third straight controversy*: Aspinall no contest on an eye poke, Pereira's back of head claims.

slides.label: The Den's Take
slides.text: A 48-47 fight is decided by inches. A fighter who *can't see straight* gives up more than inches.

slides.label: The Fix
slides.text: Refs can already take a point. If the sport wants fewer eye pokes, *the first one has to cost something*.

question: Should Goddard have taken a point for the eye poke?

caption_instagram:
Gane Hokit eye poke is the only thing anyone's talking about since UFC 334, even though Ciryl Gane kept his heavyweight belt 48-47 over Josh Hokit at Madison Square Garden.

Hokit spent fight week wearing goggles, a joke about Gane's foul history. Then in round 1, Gane's fingers caught his eye, referee Marc Goddard never called it, and Hokit says he fought the next 25 minutes seeing triple, still pinning the champ on the fence.

All three judges had it by a single round. The Den's take: a 48-47 fight is decided by inches, and a fighter who can't see straight gives up more than that. Refs can already take a point. Maybe it's time they did.

Should Goddard have taken a point for the eye poke?

caption_linkedin:
Ciryl Gane kept the UFC heavyweight title 48-47 over Josh Hokit at Madison Square Garden. But the story everyone's replaying is an eye poke referee Marc Goddard never called in round 1, one Hokit says left him seeing triple for the rest of the fight.

For founders and operators, there's a lesson under the headline. Hokit didn't cry foul or call anyone a cheater. He documented it, screenshot and all, and asked for the rematch in public, tagging the decision makers directly. That's how you make a case when the system doesn't catch something in real time: you keep the receipts and you ask for the fix.

Gane's last two title fights both ended in controversy too, a no contest on an eye poke and accusations of illegal shots. One incident is an accident. A pattern is a rules problem the UFC has not solved.

Should the ref have taken a point?
